reviews.text: Dr Ken Jones has been my vet for about 45 years.  I’ll follow him wherever he goes.

I go out of my way to travel to Overland Vet Clinic for my dog's healthcare because of their care and competence. I have seen several different vets and all have been attentive and thorough. It's not a corporate-held entity, which is becoming rare these days.

I’ve been coming here for more than 10 years through multiple dogs. But I just can’t anymore. Every time I bring my dogs in, I see a new doctor. They act like I’m a total stranger. Can’t even get my dogs name right when they’re staring at the chart. I just don’t get the feeling like anybody cares anymore. Sucks

Though my cat is terrified of his own shadow, a miraculous thing happened yesterday when I took him to see his new vet, Dr. Chavers. My cat was suddenly happy! He was relaxed, curious, friendly. He let himself to be fondled, poked and prodded by Nathalie, the tech, who was a cat-whisperer; and then by Dr. Chavers, who was everything you'd want your pet's vet to be. Compassionate, effective, professional, and warm. I've been bringing my boy, Axl, to Overland Veterinary Clinic since I adopted him 6 years ago. I've never been disappointed.
Excellent vet
Accommodating and efficient.  It's also a good sign when your dog is (mostly) comfortable when going to the Vet.  You know that your pet is being shown love and respect while being treated.

Kudos to the front office (support staff) at Overland Veterinary Clinic (OVC)! They are very efficient, caring & always professional. In particular, Sarah gave me excellent advice regarding getting my cat to take her oral medication. The doctors at OVC are excellent as well but you’re only as strong as your support staff. So keep delivering quality health care at every level & you will continue to promote loyalty to your smoothly run veterinary clinic.

We have been taking our pets to the OVC since 1993!  Dr. Schwartz was the best vet we have ever known.  We moved to Riverside in 2021 and even though we have plenty of vets there, nothing compares to this clinic.  Even though Dr. Schwartz has retired the place has the same vibe and  continues the legacy!    In addition to great vets, they have the best dental care for your pet, non-anesthetic procedure that does the job.  Our last experience was superb and we will definitely be back.

A neighbor recommended Dr Jones because he is good and charges very reasonable. I appreciate that when I walk in it feels like a private only owned vet and not a corporation. Dr Jones was able to do an ultrasound inhouse and diagnose my cat's issue right away, tell me what I needed to do and he answered ALL my questions. I was able to purchase the dietary food there as well - I think for less or the same price as retail outlets. I found my vet. 5 stars.

I will continue taking my cats to Dr. Natasha for years to come! Thanks Dr. Natasha! :)

Like the older male vet

I've had an interesting experience with Overland Veterinary Clinic. Some of the vets are very kind, and I genuinely love Dr. Natasha. Other Vets have been less so, and one of which was a little too brutally honest and I wish she was a little more sensitive in how she speaks to customers/clients.

My main issue with the clinic has been the extraordinary amount of appointments I've had to bring my cat in for. He is FIV+ and is dealing with an issue, but it seems as if after MONTHS of treatment and antibiotics, nothing has helped. I've spent thousands of dollars and my cat is still sick and suffering. He also was diagnosed with a heart murmur, which I noticed other reviews say that their pets were given these diagnoses only to also be referred to a cardiologist.

Ironically, it wasn't until the cardiologist (at the VCA) told me, that I was aware that my cat could not qualify for Pet Insurance since he was already diagnosed with the murmur. I would have hoped I had known or had been given some advice when I first brought him in to Overland Veterinary Clinic, since he is FIV+ and was told that it should not impact his health much.

It often feels like half my appointments are arbitrary and yield the same results every time I'm told to come in to move forward with a procedure. (Nothing is done, they simply just give me new medications for him.) I understand there is a process and that veterinary care in general requires expensive and specialized equipment/labs, but sometimes it feels as if every appointment is just a money-suck that leads to no results.

That said, I really can appreciate the thoroughness in which the vets conduct their work, especially because my cat does have some underlying health issues. They are meticulous and Dr. Natasha is extremely kind and cares so much for the animals. (She is the only reason I haven't tried to find a new vet.) I just wish that it wasn't so expensive, especially given that my cat has yet to get better. (He has been to the vet nearly 4+ times since he first got sick MONTHS ago.) Going here just makes me wish I had pet insurance.

Overall, these are my own personal experiences. I understand different pets have different needs, and my case may be an exception. Nevertheless, I hope this is useful feedback for the Clinic, and helpful advice to any current or possible customers.

I’ve been searching for a new Veterinary Clinic that was closer to where I live. I have an older dog that I cherish, and I wanted to find someone knowledgeable and compassionate. I can’t believe the good fortune that I have had in finding Overland Veterinary Clinic. The girls at the front desk are so friendly and helpful. The place is so clean And the furniture so practical and aesthetically, beautiful, and the best thing of all is that it doesn’t smell like other veterinary centers. With that horrible like rancid fruit aroma from disinfectant. What a fantastic place. The vet that we met with was just brilliant. One by one she crossed off deep concerns I had about issues with my dog. She knew exactly what was going on. I feel so much better now. I am so glad I found this place. A wonderful place where there is respect and honor given to animals as they deserve.

Not cheap, but very thorough. For my 12 years old cat: dental work, 3 extractions with anesthesia, meds, removal of a lump + biopsy: about $2,000+. Clean and friendly place. Usually on time. Free parking.
Had a female Dr. can not remember her name but she spent 50 minutes on initial visit and was extremely thorough.

I won't be back to this vet. Each time I come with my dog, I have to wait beyond what is normal and certainly much longer of a wait than I've had at any other vet office. Last time I came I waited for an hour, I left without seeing a vet because I had to go back to work and then received a call apologizing and telling me that someone forgot to inform the vet that I was sitting in the little room waiting. I thought I'd give it one more try and this time I sat in in the waiting , and I was the only person in the waiting room then I sat in the small little room waiting for 25 minutes with no one giving me the courtesy of letting me know that they were running behind or that someone would be with me soon. Nothing! I left and there still wasn't anybody in the waiting room so not sure why they couldn't see my dog any respectable amount of time considering they were not busy at all. I'm sure they're good at what they do but their customer service is horrible and there are plenty of other good vets out there that would be willing to treat a new customer much better.
We're thrilled to hear about your positive experience at Overland Veterinary Clinic! Thank you for your feedback.

Such a great local vet! Staff is friendly and helpful and doctors are knowledgeable and kind!

We brought our 15yo tabby cat in last minute in a Saturday because he had lost a lost of weight and was having a hard time eating and swallowing. We first went to the VCA who said he probably had a tooth abscess and would need several extractions amounting to over $5k. We came to OVC for a second opinion. Dr jones took a look and told us with pragmatism, directness and compassion that it was most likely oral squamous cell carcinoma. He answered all our questions about treatment and outlined all the options but never once did he deceive us into believe it was a good diagnosis. His transparency and bedside manner was so professional and we are forever grateful for being so kind and straightforward. He helped us prepare to make our boy comfortable and gave us options to ease his pain. It was perhaps the best delivery of bad news one can hope for and we are so grateful.

Edit: received a hand-written condolences card from Dr. Jones after our sweet boy passed. The thoughtfulness is unparalleled

I used to recommend this place widely but over the years it has gone downhill and now, I have moved to another vet. The constant spam and promotions are incessant with no way to opt-out. They are constantly selling. I used to drive 30 minutes out of the way to come here and paid more because I wanted to support a small business, but this was an era that is no longer when it was operated by someone else. I don't know what happened but I don't recommend this vet anymore.

Though the doctor I saw and the nurse were nice it doesn’t make up for how expensive a simple vet visit was. They charged me $7 to dispose of the needle they used - $112 for a shot that is usually $80 max I’ve paid for at previous facilities. On top of that, they also charged me a $95 vet visit when they knew I just needed a shot. They also didn’t sweep the floor in the room from the previous animal that was in there before letting me in with my cat who already has a compromised immune system and is completely indoor. Unfortunately my usual vet is in between facilities at the moment so I thought I could come back to where I use to go pre pandemic comfortably but now I will never come back and I never would recommend for how unnecessarily expensive it is and cleanliness. Keep your pets safe and your wallets.

Today, I took my guinea pig to this clinic for a treatment. First of all, we arrived at the clinic on time, but the doctor was delayed by 30 minutes. Second, this clinic is not qualified to see guinea pigs at all. How to say, the nurse measured the weight of my guinea pig was 1.07 pounds. I saw the scale say this with my own eyes, but what she recorded was 1.43. Third, we explained to the doctor that our guinea pig had symptoms of sneezing. The doctor did not look at whether her nose had a runny nose, but concluded very perfunctorily that it was pneumonia. And he also said that the pets brought back by the pet store usually have this problem. Excuse me, have you really looked at my pet seriously? The process was very unpleasant. The doctor grabbed my guinea pig very hard. The final checkout price is also very outrageous. I will never go to this hospital again. If you can only see cats and dogs, don't take pets other than cats and dogs! The hospital is extremely unrecommended.

Overall, unprofessional interactions and I'm not convinced my cat got a quality care.

I came to Overland for an ultrasound thinking my dog likely had pancreatic cancer based on lab results from her current vet (they don't have an ultrasound machine).  I could see the wheels turning as Dr. Jones examined her and reviewed the lab results I had brought with me.  Something wasn't adding up; if her glucose was that low, she would have been very symptomatic, if not dead (it was that low).  He suggested we start with another glucose test.  It came back well within normal range.  Given the extreme difference in results, he suggested we repeat the test later that day.  I went home, fed her lunch, and returned 3 hours later for an apples to apples comparison with other vet's repeat test.  Her glucose was perfect. Overland is more expensive, but I have prior history with Dr. Jones.  I will just have to make adjustments in my finances for her to be able to continue seeing him.

The first time I took my cat to the clinic was in 2022 for a regular checkup. The doctor was friendly and we got the vaccines and revolution plus. My impression is that the doctor likes to recommend treatments/ products that I of course can’t tell if are over treatments. For example, the doctor would suggest a dental cleaning for my cat. But it’s not that bad because the doctor didn’t try that hard to sell. I later found out that the clinic charged twice as much than the chewy price for revolution plus. This is understandable because the clinic has a financial incentive.

What pissed me off and made me decide to give this review is what happened when I later took my cat because she vomited. It was also my bad that I still came to this clinic although I kind of got the idea that this clinic had a strong financial incentive to charge people. I came just because it’s close to my apt.

It was with Dr Forsythe. First, he unsurprisingly recommended many tests, like blood work, x ray and feces test. I hesitated because I know it’ll cost a lot and I tried to decide what test to get based on what time I can get the results. For example, if it can be seen through x ray that my cat had something in the stomach, then maybe I can skip the feces work.

But Dr forsythe gave very wrong estimates of timelines. He said we can get the X ray results within 2h and blood work may take a whole afternoon. So after we learnt that there’s nothing in the stomach from x ray after 4h, I decided to move on to the blood work. Actually I had to take my cat back because it was getting too late and by this time I was informed that the clinic can’t get the results that day. But they promised I’ll hear back in two days.

So I took my cat home without any diagnosis. She got the standard treatment for vomiting including hydration injection and some vitamin in the clinic.

Dr Forsythe also prescribed one week’s antibiotics and metronidazole. They were compounded and cost 500$. Actually it took time for the pharmacy to compound it and I can only get them the third day. By the time I got these medications, my cat already stopped vomiting.

But i didn’t want to waste the expensive medicine and decided to feed my cat anyway. The medication process is frustrating. Before we left the clinic, Dr Forsythe gave me the number and agreed that I can text him when I have any updates and questions about my cat. But I find an interesting pattern. My first question was that my cat started to drool a lot when I medicated her. It was fine the doctor responded within one hour.

But the following days, when I had questions, he stopped answering. I think I was very polite and tried not to be angry. Then he agreed to give me a call that Friday. Of course he didn’t.

I tested my hypothesis that this Dr Forsythe was only interested in questions that potentially can bring him more income. So I texted him if I should take my cat sometime back for annual checkup and vaccines. Oh he responded right away!!!

In The meantime, the clinic kept saying they didn’t get the result each time I called. It ended up taking A WHOLE WEEK!

So the Dr finally send the full health record and diagnosis after a week. He can’t give any clear diagnosis but suspected IBD.

I had medical background. I don’t know since when IBD becomes a cure-all diagnosis.

It took me a year to decide to write this review because i don’t want to mistakenly accuse someone. During this year, I received promotion emails from overland, saying my cat needs this, needs that.

But the clinic I now go for my cat, the vet never recommends extra treatments. I then understand that not all vets are like Dr Forsythe, and not clinics are like this overland clinic. I hope other people can learn from my sad experience. I just graduated at that time and started a new job. This visit cost me a lot financially.

I’ve been bringing my dog here for the past 3 years, they have always been helpful and through with the visits, but after my most recent visit, I feel disappointed and taken advantage of. I brought my dog in because I suspected a UTI, and was charged $805.86—a shockingly high amount for a relatively straightforward issue.

Here’s the breakdown:
•	Exam: $97
•	Urinalysis: $200
•	Urine Culture & MIC: $382
•	Waste Fee: $6.50
•	Medicated Pads: $26
•	Clavamox: $94.36

When I went to pay, the total came up to nearly $900, which was $100 more than what had been previously quoted to me. I had to speak up, and only then did they double-check and correct the error.

After doing some research and speaking with other pet owners and vets, it seems many of these charges—especially the urine culture and MIC—may not have been necessary, particularly since my dog doesn’t have a history of UTIs and the test results weren’t concerning.

I’m deeply frustrated by this experience. I trusted this clinic with my dog’s care for years, but this feels like overcharging for unnecessary services. My dog never had a UTI before so I didn’t know better.
